outcome: Project sites and roaming staff get the same identity-driven security policy without a bespoke build at every location.
overview: A construction group’s workforce is defined by project sites rather than offices: a site compound stands up for eighteen months with whatever connectivity is available, and design, planning and finance staff move between them. Prisma Access inspects that traffic in the vendor’s cloud so the same policy applies at a site compound, a head office and a laptop in a hotel. The design question that decides the outcome is not which points of presence exist, but whether anyone has written down which applications the project teams actually use and who is entitled to reach each of them.

benefits.text: Project sites get enterprise-grade inspection without an inspection stack at each compound
benefits.limits: Depends on the site having usable internet; where connectivity is the constraint, moving inspection to cloud does not fix it

benefits.text: Access to project systems is granted per application, so a lost device does not expose a network
benefits.limits: Applies to applications the access proxy can publish; site systems using legacy protocols may still need a network path and should be listed as exceptions

benefits.text: A site compound can be stood up and torn down without a bespoke security build each time
benefits.limits: The control plane is vendor-operated, so tenant region and log residency are design decisions to be made and recorded explicitly rather than properties of the product

residency: Inspection and log storage happen in vendor-operated regions; the tenant region is selected explicitly at design and recorded, because it is a compliance decision rather than a default

notFor.situation: A group already migrated onto another cloud-delivered secure access service
notFor.why: Policy does not port between services, so the estate would be authored twice for one outcome

notFor.situation: An organisation whose staff work only from inspected offices
notFor.why: The service addresses users away from the perimeter; where there are none it adds a hop and a subscription

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Palo Alto Networks implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a migrated pilot population with policy under change control
Support model: Vendor subscription support for the service; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed policy operations.
1) Assessment — application and population inventory, identity readiness, residency position
2) Design — policy model, service location and log region, publication plan and fallback
3) Pilot — one project population migrated with the legacy path retained and measured
4) Migrate and hand over — remaining populations migrated, legacy platform decommissioned
deliverables: A user in any population receives the same policy decision for the same application
A published project system is unreachable by network path, verified by attempting it
Logs for every population are queryable in one place within the chosen region

languages: English delivery; Arabic site documentation on request
